target: route "degenerate" — Degenerate one-player games: ties as a resource, and a run longer than the Holt-Klee ceiling with one player

findings.defect: The statement is strictly stronger than the argument: what is proved is that no one-player stopping SSG with |Vmax|=5 has an all-switches run OF LENGTH 12 whose resolution lies in the orbit of s12; the printed statement drops "of length 12" and so also asserts the impossibility of a SHORT run whose (corner-)resolution happens to lie in that orbit, which the (F1)-(F4) filter does not touch because (F2) is imposed only at the walk vertices, and a shorter walk imposes fewer constraints.
findings.evidence: The proof's only computational input is "the only starts of length 12 are 0 and 16", which is vacuous for a start whose walk is shorter. I reproduced every computation exactly (five.py): s12 is a USO, acyclic, BA height 12, not Holt-Klee; walk from 0 = [0,15,24,31,20,23,18,14,26,10,2,3,1]; walk lengths from all 32 starts = [12,0,2,1,10,8,4,5,8,4,3,7,5,11,5,11,12,2,6,3,8,4,6,7,10,8,4,7,7,9,5,9] so only 0 and 16 give 12; the seven (F1)-blocks of dimension >=1 are exactly {0,16},{1,3},{12,14},{13,15},{14,30},{18,22},{29,31}; 96 candidate partitions; the unique nontrivial (F1)-(F4) partition is {0,16} at start 0 and there is none at start 16. GAP (one sentence): "No one-player stopping SSG with |Vmax|=5 whose all-switches run is SHORTER than 12 can have a corner resolution in the orbit of s12." Fix: insert "of length 12" into the statement.

findings.defect: The second sentence — "cor:seven-two-player holds without its nondegeneracy hypothesis" — is not equivalent to what is proved. cor:seven-two-player is about the improvement ORIENTATION lying in the height-seven orbit; for a degenerate game that orientation is undefined and only a corner resolution exists, and the theorem excludes only a RUN of length 7, not a degenerate game whose resolution lies in the orbit while every run is shorter. (The third clause, "the two Min vertices of G# are necessary for any game realising the height-seven orbit AS A RUN", is correct.)
findings.evidence: thm-no-seven's proof begins "Suppose G is such a game, with run sigma_0,...,sigma_7" and uses cor:ceiling-general to force height(s') = 7 from the run's length; nothing in it constrains a game whose resolution has height 7 but whose runs are all shorter. The main theorem itself is sound: I rebuilt every input independently — enum4.c gives 5541744 USOs of the 4-cube, 4792176 acyclic, height distribution (by translation class x16) 16/264608/1800000/2072832/599424/54912/384, so h*(4)=7 attained by exactly 384 outmaps; seven.py shows those 384 are precisely the free orbit of (0,1,3,6,7,4,13,10,14,15,9,12,11,8,5,2), none Holt-Klee (max-flow 2 on the whole 4-cube where 4 are needed), while (0,1,3,2,5,14,7,4,13,10,11,12,9,6,15,8) is HK of height 6, so h*_HK(4)=6; and the (F1)-(F4) enumeration gives exactly 768 (outmap,start) pairs of walk length 7, exactly 384 admitting a nontrivial partition, in each case unique and the single edge {sigma_0, sigma_0 xor e_x} at the start, with exactly four (F1)-blocks of dimension >=1 per outmap, all edges, pairwise disjoint. I also checked that each of (F1)-(F4) is NECESSARY for the flat partition of a real game (from lem:flat-class(a)/(c), thm:flat-resolution, lem:face-sink), so the filter cannot over-exclude.

findings.defect: "the run has 24 acyclic unique sink completions of its partial orientation, 17 of them Holt-Klee" is false as literally stated: the partial orientation (S,D) has 96 AUSO completions, 74 of them Holt-Klee. 24 (17 HK) is the number of completions that additionally AGREE WITH THE RUN, i.e. satisfy s(sigma_t)=S_t at the three run vertices.
findings.evidence: nolin2.py/nolin3.py, exact: the seven flat edges are (0,2,dir1),(0,4,dir2),(2,6,dir2),(4,6,dir1),(5,7,dir1),(12,14,dir1),(13,15,dir1); of the 2^7 orientations, 96 give a USO that is acyclic, 74 of those are Holt-Klee; splitting by whether s(7)=S[7] and s(13)=S[13] gives (keeps run, HK) counts {(True,True):17, (True,False):7, (False,True):57, (False,False):15}, i.e. exactly 24 keeping the run and 17 of those HK. Everything else in prop-nolin reproduces exactly from the printed rows (nolin.py): S=[9,10,9,8,9,12,9,12,5,4,7,6,1,0,1,0], D=[6,0,6,0,6,2,6,2,0,0,0,0,2,2,2,2], run 7->11->13, y^15-y^13 = (61360/43111)(y^7-y^5) with both differences supported on coordinates (x2,0),(x2,1),(x3,1) only, hence (*) is genuinely infeasible; (**) is feasible (gpert.py finds an admissible (pi,rho) with Delta = -23/10 and -2629/4538); and "34 vertices, 28 average" is exactly right — the minimum number of average vertices per row (collapsed fair-coin tree, exact DP) is 4,3,4,4,4,4,0,5 = 28.

findings.defect: The clause "for m=2,3,4 the value is already attained by a DEGENERATE game" is not established at m=3 and m=4: the two witnesses deg_m3_run4.json and deg_m4_run6.json are harmonic normal forms, not games, and their q-entries are NOT dyadic (denominators 27305639040 = 2^7 x 213325305 and 4510476448 = 2^5 x 140952389). Turning a normal form into a fair-coin SSG is the normal-form dictionary (v4), which the standing repository lists as UNVERIFIED; and for these odd parts any realisation needs a cyclic average gadget whose size is the multiplicative order of 2 modulo an odd number of order 10^8, so the "explicit instances" are neither explicit nor small.
findings.evidence: degjson.py rebuilds both files exactly: both are stopping (every row leaks), runs 6->3->5->1->0 (length 4, flat class {4,6} on the run) and 0->15->8->13->1->5->4 (length 6, flat class {10,11} off it), matching the claims — but the denominator sets are {1,256,512,1024,27305639040} and {1,32,64,128,256,512,1024,4510476448}. REPAIR (verified by me, exact): the clause is TRUE and has explicit dyadic witnesses already inside frontier.tex. prop:overshoot-small's game G'=B'_7 is a one-player stopping SSG on 182 vertices with |Vmax|=4; I rebuilt it and reproduced its run of length 6, switched sets {0,3},{0,1,2},{0,1},{1},{2},{3}, and final val(0)=34611559809/37019025280 — and it is DEGENERATE, with D(sigma_0)={1,2}. Freezing its Max vertex 2 at its second edge (retyping it as an average vertex with both successors = vertex 1) gives an explicit degenerate one-player stopping SSG with |Vmax|=3 whose all-switches run from (1,1,0) is (1,1,0)->(0,1,1)->(1,0,1)->(0,0,1)->(0,0,0), length 4, with a single flat incidence at the start. The equality h*_1 = h*_HK = 1,2,4,6 itself is unaffected: I verified the lower bounds from explicit fair-coin games (B1_game.json, N=58, max run 4; AP_m4_k0_den256_s200_game.json, N=100, nondegenerate, max run 6) and the upper bounds from the census (m<=3: h*_HK=h*=1,2,4, verified by full enumeration) and thm-no-seven.

findings.defect: The concluding sentence "In particular no amount of chaining raises the run length above m+O(1)" over-reaches the corollary's own hypotheses, which assume (i) every block of B_r is dead until B_r wakes, (ii) a block's vertices never switch while dead, and (iii) NO vertex of B_1..B_{r-1} switches after B_r wakes. (iii) is precisely the non-interleaving assumption that a superlinear serial construction would violate, so the corollary bounds a restricted family of chains, not chaining in general.
findings.evidence: The proof uses (iii) twice: to conclude "after round T only B_r moves" and to apply lem:subgame to the frozen subgame. Nothing in the proof rules out a chain in which an early block resumes switching after a later block wakes. The rest of the corollary is correct: I checked that freezing Vmax\Vmax(B_r) and retyping the frozen Max vertices as average vertices with coinciding out-edges preserves stopping (the trap condition for an avg vertex with equal successors is the controlled-vertex condition) and all values (lem:subgame(b)), and that the numerical h*_1(k)-k = 0,0,1,2 for k<=4 follows from degen:cor-hstar-one.

findings.defect: (a) asserts "X(G) is a simple m-polytope", which needs X(G) BOUNDED; neither degen:prop-partial-lp nor the prop:oneplayer-lp proof it cites "verbatim" argues boundedness. (It is true.) Separately, (c)'s "the flat classes are exactly the faces of X(G) on which obj is constant" is wrong as stated, since every sub-face of a flat class is also a face on which obj is constant; it should read "the MAXIMAL faces on which obj is constant", which is what the proof establishes.
findings.evidence: GAP (one sentence): "On a stopping one-player SSG the recession cone of X(G) is trivial." Proof sketch (mine, not in the route): summing the equalities over w gives sum_{v,a} y_{v,a}(1 - ||p^{v,a}||_1) = 0 for a recession direction, so y is supported on leak-free actions; the set U of Max vertices carrying such a positive coordinate is closed under the first-passage supports of those actions, and U together with the average vertices its actions visit is a nonempty trap, contradicting lem:trapchar. Everything else in prop-partial-lp I verified computationally with zero violations: over 150 random one-player m=4 games (18 degenerate) x 16 strategies, obj(y^sigma) = sum_v val_sigma(v), y^sigma >= 1, the three-case sign law S/D/neither, and "flat classes = level sets of sigma -> val_sigma = subcubes with direction set D" all hold (sweep.py); all 692 corner resolutions in that sample are AUSOs, confirming thm:flat-resolution.

findings.defect: Two asserted steps. (i) "Condition (*) of degen:lem-perturb is the case pi = 0 of (**)" holds in only one direction: (**) with pi=0 yields (*) for d = <rho,.>, but (*) permits an ARBITRARY linear functional d while (**) forces rho_{v,a} >= 0 wherever q^{v,a} = 0, and adding a constant to all coordinates of d does not preserve the differences (sum_v y^sigma_v is not constant in sigma). (ii) The conclusion says "the game with rows (p+eps(...), q+eps(...)) is a nondegenerate one-player stopping SSG", i.e. it silently uses the normal-form-to-game direction of the UNVERIFIED (v4) dictionary; prop:oneplayer-lp is then applied to that game.
findings.evidence: Neither point damages the headline: degen:thm-no-seven uses only degen:cor-onetie, whose functional d(y)=y_{x,a} IS admissible (rho_{x,a}=1>=0, all other rho = 0), and it perturbs only the objective on the ORIGINAL game's polytope, never the game. lem-gperturb is used only for rem-star's sweeps. I independently confirmed the derivative computation (u_sigma = d/deps val^eps_sigma solves u = P_sigma u + pi_sigma val_sigma + rho_sigma, so u_sigma = (I-P_sigma)^{-1}(pi_sigma val_sigma + rho_sigma), exactly as printed) and confirmed (**) is feasible on the degen:prop-nolin run by exact search over the admissible cone (gpert.py).

verdict:
SOUND. Nothing fatal or major survived. The headline — degen:thm-no-seven, hence h*_1(4) = h*_HK(4) = 6 — stands, and so do degen:thm-timer, degen:prop-staircase and degen:prop-family.

WHAT I REBUILT INDEPENDENTLY (all in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-degenerate-correctness/, exact rational arithmetic, written from the statements, no route code imported):
(1) enum4.c — the FULL exhaustive census of the 4-cube (not read from the route's census file): 5 541 744 USOs, 4 792 176 acyclic, height counts 16, 264 608, 1 800 000, 2 072 832, 599 424, 54 912, 384 for heights 1..7. So h*(4)=7 with exactly 384 outmaps, which seven.py shows to be exactly the free orbit of the route's representative; none is Holt-Klee (max flow 2 on the whole cube where 4 are needed) and a height-6 HK witness exists, so h*_HK(4)=6. Independent Python census for m=1,2,3: 2/12/744 USOs, 2/12/728 AUSOs, h*=1,2,4, h*_HK=1,2,4.
(2) flat.py+seven.py — my own (F1)-(F4) enumerator reproduces degen:lem-seven-flat exactly: 768 pairs of walk length 7, exactly 384 admit a nontrivial partition, each unique and the single edge at the START; four (F1)-blocks of dimension >=1 per outmap, all edges, pairwise disjoint (16 candidates). I also checked each of (F1)-(F4) is NECESSARY for a real game's flat partition, so the filter cannot over-exclude.
(3) five.py — every claim about s12 on the 5-cube reproduces.
(4) nf.py+nolin*.py+gpert.py — degen:prop-nolin rebuilt from the printed rows: S, D, run 7->11->13, the exact constant 61360/43111, the genuine infeasibility of (*), the feasibility of (**), and even "34 vertices, 28 average" (minimum collapsed-tree cost = 28).
(5) fam.py+ssg2.py — all five rows of degen:prop-family's table, plus s=1,2,3, at the normal-form level AND from a rebuilt explicit fair-coin game with a different block; B's N=123/a=117 confirmed by an independent minimal-average-vertex count.
(6) the staircase from the game at k=1,2,4,8,16,24 (plain and leaky); explicit lower-bound witnesses B1_game (N=58, run 4) and AP_m4_k0_den256_s200_game (N=100, nondegenerate, run 6); prop:overshoot-small rebuilt from frontier.tex (run 6, switched sets, final value 34611559809/37019025280 all match).
(7) timer.py — 2936 wake events on random one-player stopping games, zero violations of T <= m or of the distinct-first-switch structure; and I reconstructed degen:thm-timer's proof line by line (the "first switch" step, the "w' dead at sigma_{s-2}" step and the iteration all check out).
(8) sweep.py — zero violations of degen:prop-partial-lp's obj identity, y>=1, three-case sign law, and flat-class = level set, over 150 random m=4 games x 16 strategies.
(9) Falsification attempts: 5001 random damped one-player m=4 games produced no run longer than 4 (nothing near 7); 20000 random m=3 games produced no degenerate run-4 instance (I found one constructively instead). Per the standing rule, this is a report, not evidence.

STANDING-ERROR SWEEP: no greedy policy iteration (all val_sigma are exact linear solves / least fixed points on games verified stopping); no dict-literal row collapse (I re-derived prop:overshoot-small, which HAS a vertex with coinciding successors, with accumulating rows and matched the paper's value); no sink-index collisions (I rebuilt the family independently); the trap for stopping and Z_sigma for deadness are both used with the right convention; no decision rule, no pair test, no Z_0/Z_1 question arises; run lengths count productive rounds only (L = |run|-1, the terminal strategy uncounted); the route claims no polynomial class and no oracle that is target-equivalent — degen:lem-perturb perturbs an objective on a polytope inside a proof, never as an algorithm.

THE ROUTE'S OWN GAP IS CORRECTLY STATED. "Every stopping SSG with Vmin empty and |Vmax|=m has all-switches runs of length at most h*_HK(m)" is not proved, and degen:prop-nolin genuinely shows the single-linear-functional route fails on some runs. The dependence on Holt-Klee's theorem and on Gaertner-Morris-Ruest is cited from memory, exactly as rem:oneplayer-lp already does; I did not check those against sources.

FOR THE INTEGRATOR: five textual fixes (insert "of length 12" in degen:prop-five; delete or restate the "Equivalently, cor:seven-two-player ..." clause in degen:thm-no-seven; say "completions agreeing with the run" in degen:prop-nolin; say "maximal faces" in degen:prop-partial-lp(c); soften degen:cor-gate's last sentence to the non-interleaving chains it covers), one added sentence for the boundedness of X(G), one honest downgrade or replacement of the degenerate-attainment witnesses in degen:cor-hstar-one (a replacement is available inside frontier.tex, as recorded above), and the two dangling labels.
